relations.note: Surabhi is named Dakṣa’s daughter in one epic genealogy.

relations.myth: Surabhi emerges from Dakṣa’s fragrant eructation
relations.note: Dakṣa produces Surabhi from his mouth after drinking nectar.
Surabhi bears Nandinī through union with Kaśyapa.
Surabhi is Nandinī’s mother through Kaśyapa.
Later retellings merge Nandinī with Kamadhenu despite their distinct epic genealogy.
Later retellings rename Vasiṣṭha’s wish-yielding cow Śabalā as Kamadhenu.

relations.myth: Vasiṣṭha’s cow sustains sacrifice and hospitality
relations.note: Nandinī or Śabalā supplies Vasiṣṭha’s rites and inexhaustible hospitality.

relations.myth: Śabalā resists Viśvāmitra’s attempted seizure
relations.note: With Vasiṣṭha’s authorization, Śabalā generates armies against the king’s forces.

relations.myth: Śabalā defeats Viśvāmitra’s forces
relations.note: Śabalā creates armies that destroy Viśvāmitra’s army and sons.

relations.myth: Dyu steals Nandinī for her miraculous milk
relations.note: Dyu steals Nandinī at his wife’s request, prompting Vasiṣṭha’s curse.

relations.myth: The Vasus steal Nandinī
relations.note: The Vasus participate in Nandinī’s theft and are cursed to human birth.

relations.myth: Gaṅgā bears the Vasus after Nandinī’s theft
relations.note: The theft indirectly causes the cursed Vasus to be born through Gaṅgā.

relations.myth: Surabhi weeps for an abused weak bullock
relations.note: Surabhi teaches Indra that maternal compassion is strongest toward the weak.

relations.myth: Surabhi and Indra consecrate Kṛṣṇa as Govinda
relations.note: Surabhi and the humbled Indra jointly perform Kṛṣṇa’s consecration.
One later epic genealogy says Brahmā directly creates Surabhi.

relations.myth: Brahmā grants Surabhi the celestial Goloka
relations.note: After Surabhi’s austerities, Brahmā grants her a realm beyond ordinary divine worlds.

relations.myth: Milk-froth provokes Śiva’s color-changing gaze
relations.note: Froth from Surabhi’s daughters touches Śiva, whose angry glance changes their colors.

relations.myth: Surabhi falsely confirms Brahmā reached the liṅga’s summit
relations.note: Surabhi supports Brahmā’s false testimony concerning Śiva’s endless fiery liṅga.

relations.myth: Śiva curses Surabhi for false testimony
relations.note: Śiva curses Surabhi or cattle after she supports Brahmā’s false claim.
Kṛṣṇa declares himself kāmadhuk, the wish-yielding cow among cattle.

relations.myth: Surabhi anoints Kṛṣṇa as Govinda
relations.note: Surabhi praises Kṛṣṇa and bathes him with milk during his consecration.

relations.myth: Kṛṣṇa manifests Surabhi from his left side
relations.note: Kṛṣṇa produces Surabhi from his body in Goloka and first worships her.

relations.myth: Airāvata assists Surabhi’s consecration of Kṛṣṇa
relations.note: Airāvata supplies celestial Gaṅgā water while Surabhi supplies milk for the consecration.

relations.myth: Divine mothers authorize Kṛṣṇa’s consecration
relations.note: Later readings say Aditi and the divine mothers direct Surabhi’s consecration of Kṛṣṇa.

relations.myth: Divine mothers authorize Kṛṣṇa’s consecration
relations.note: Later interpretations make the divine mothers direct Surabhi’s consecration of Kṛṣṇa.

relations.myth: Sages receive Surabhi after the ocean churning
relations.note: The sages accept Surabhi because her milk products and ghee sustain sacrifice.

relations.myth: Jamadagni keeps the miraculous wish-cow
relations.note: Later Purāṇic accounts make Kamadhenu or Homadhenu the cow sustaining Jamadagni’s hermitage.

relations.myth: Kārtavīrya seizes Jamadagni’s wish-cow
relations.note: Later accounts make the king’s desire for Kamadhenu central to the conflict.

relations.myth: Cow seizure precipitates Paraśurāma’s campaigns
relations.note: The later Kamadhenu seizure contributes indirectly to Paraśurāma’s war against kṣatriyas.
Kamadhenu accompanies Dattātreya in later iconography without an early continuous narrative encounter.
Nineteenth-century artists combined Kamadhenu’s imagery with Burāq’s female head and wings.
